subject: Run 2 on Part 8: the conflict is real, the magnitude was overstated threefold
body:
Second-run result on the one claim that would have overturned FORGE UNIFIED III's whole
quantitative case. I did this by hand because the agent doing it was killed by a rate limit.

The claim was: Part 8's b = 3.09 is built on the MEAN of a heavy tail, in violation of the
document's own rule that you must size on the MEDIAN -- and that correcting it takes the
conservative stack from +0.219R to -0.339R, inverting every compounding figure.

What I found, rederiving it from the document's own numbers:

THE TABLE'S ARITHMETIC IS FINE. E = p*b - (1-p) reproduces every published cell exactly.
Break-even at b=3.09 is 24.45% against a published 24.5%. The sums are right. Calling these
"arithmetic errors" overstates it -- what is contestable is a modelling choice.

THE MEDIAN CONFLICT IS REAL. Three separate rules say size on the median, and every Part 8
table uses one mean-flavoured b.

BUT THE SIZE OF IT WAS OVERSTATED THREEFOLD. The claimed 2.52x factor appears nowhere in your
document. Your own line reports median 64.8p against mean 78.1p -- a ratio of 1.205. Applying
that:

    b            3.09  ->  2.56
    break-even  24.45% -> 28.06%
    E at 25%    +0.022 -> -0.109      <- flips, so the direction was right
    E at 30%    +0.227 -> +0.069      <- still positive
    E at 35%    +0.431 -> +0.247      <- still positive

So the conservative row does invert, and that matters. But "every compounding figure inverts"
is not what your numbers produce.

One thing I could not settle: whether b = 3.09 is itself mean-derived. The 14p/35% row implies a
43.3p reward, which matches neither your median nor your mean directly, so there is an
intermediate step the extract does not show. If b is already a median figure, the objection
dissolves entirely. Naming it rather than assuming.

That is what the second run is for. The first found a real problem and then exaggerated it; both
halves are the answer.
